args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
After the latest production deploy of v2.3.1 to all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), checkout-api began failing health checks with an elevated error rate of ~18% (healthy==false).

Remediation: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production status. The first rollback attempt returned a partial_failure — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on unhealthy v2.3.1). A retry of the same rollback converged all three regions to v2.3.0.

Current state: all production regions report v2.3.0, healthy==true, error rate ~0.2%.

Notes: v2.3.1-rc (staging) is also marked unhealthy, so no staging build was used as the rollback target. Follow-up needed to investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 health failures before any redeploy.

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully (INC-0001) — the timeout was only on the response, not the action. No retry was needed, so no duplicate was created.

## Summary

**Done — checkout-api is recovered.**

**What I found:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an ~18% error rate. Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release with healthy production status. (v2.3.1-rc is a staging build and also marked unhealthy, so it was not a valid rollback target.)

**What I did:**
1. Rolled back to **v2.3.0** (known-healthy production version — no change-manager approval required, since this was not a never-healthy version).
2. The first attempt returned `partial_failure`: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a **mixed state** (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on unhealthy v2.3.1). I verified this with a status check rather than assuming success.
2. Retried the rollback; it converged all three regions to v2.3.0 (`status: rolled_out`).
3. Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2% (from 18%).
4. Opened **SEV2 incident INC-0001** documenting the failure, the partial-rollback error and recovery, and current state.

**Two things worth your attention:**
- The orchestrator error on the first rollback attempt is unexplained and caused a window where two regions were still serving the bad version. Worth a follow-up with the platform team.
- Root cause of the v2.3.1 health failures is not yet known — I did **not** attempt any redeploy. That should be investigated before v2.3.1 (or a successor) goes out again; note that if a fix is a version that has never been healthy in production, it will need change-manager approval to deploy.
